1.content: When evaluating a candidate move, first enumerate all possible stochastic outcomes of that move, including slips that may leave the agent in the same cell. If any outcome would place the agent on a hazardous (H) cell, move the agent out of the grid, or leave the agent stationary, apply an extremely large negative penalty (e.g., –1,000,000) to the move's score before any other bonuses. This safety penalty overrides all other heuristics and is applied regardless of the probability of the unsafe outcome, ensuring the move is never selected.

4.content: After applying the Safety Heuristic (which penalizes any move that lands on a hazardous (H) cell, exits the grid, or leaves the agent stationary), score moves based on their effect on Manhattan distance to the goal: assign higher scores to moves that strictly decrease the distance, lower scores to moves that increase it, and neutral scores to moves that leave the distance unchanged. Additionally, subtract a modest penalty (e.g., -10) for moves that bring the agent closer to a known hazard cell; this penalty is applied after safety checks and cannot override the safety penalty.

5.content: Ensure the enumeration of stochastic outcomes includes the possibility of a slip that leaves the agent in the same cell. If such a stay‑in‑place outcome exists for a move, treat the move as unsafe and apply the large negative safety penalty, regardless of its probability.
